thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: autopage fired for service=canary-runner env=prod - 5xx spike and SIGTERM seen across ~30% of canary pods. alert_id=CNRY-8472

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-9921 -> oncall-sre. Initial severity: P1. Escalation policy: canary-deployments.

oncall-sre: acked. I’m jumping in - adding bridge. ops-bridge-bot has joined the channel.

ashwin: seeing repeated `SIGTERM` in canary pods logs, not OOM. stack shows graceful shutdowns triggered by `shutdown_watchdog`.

maria: rollouts just pushed 3 minutes before alert - release id=rl-optimizer-2026-03-15. Can we confirm which commit?

sam: confirmed commit 4a7b2f6 - added async scheduler and background worker that touches shared GPU allocator.

emily: load looks normal, but p95 latency on canary model generation jumps and then pods disappear with SIGTERM. Could be watchdog detecting stuck loop and terminating.

oncall-sre: quick ask: can we divert traffic from canary to stable? If yes, do it now.

maria: initiating traffic diversion: set traffic.split.canary=0 -> command: `rwctl rollout traffic --service canary-runner --set-canary 0`

ashwin: running `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=canary-runner -o wide` shows many pods in Terminating state. grabbing recent pod logs:```
[2026-03-15T02:14:12Z] ERROR runtime: watchdog detected stuck job, sending SIGTERM to pid 2345
[2026-03-15T02:14:13Z] INFO cleanup: closing KV cache
[2026-03-15T02:14:13Z] WARN eviction: GPU allocator freed 0.2GB, failing gracefully
```

oncall-sre: thanks. This looks like the new background worker triggers watchdog on longer tail requests. Suggest rollback to previous image and scale set to stable.

sam: starting rollback: `rwctl release rollback --service canary-runner --to-version rl-optimizer-2026-03-10`  

pagerduty-bot: PD-9921 -> acknowledged by oncall-sre (oncall-sre). Pager escalations paused.

emily: patch/rollback initiated, controller reports rollout started. Current stable pods healthy.

maria: scaling canary down to 0 manually as extra safety: `kubectl scale deployment/canary-runner --replicas=0 -n prod`

oncall-sre: monitoring health checks and error rate. Any customer-facing impact?

ashwin: quick check of error budget graphs: embedding/serving errors spike correlates with canary-traffic window. We diverted before full rollout so impact limited to ~120 requests/min over 3 minutes. No broader customer reports in Zendesk.

sam: telemetry shows ~0.02% of overall traffic hit the buggy canary during the 3m window. Low but we should still note in incident summary.

emily: running smoke checks against stable: all OK.

oncall-sre: good. Next steps: capture diagnostics, open PR revert + postmortem. Who will own rollback PR?

maria: I’ll open the revert PR, add tests to prevent background worker from touching allocator under canary flag. Tagging @sam for code review.

ashwin: saving pod core logs and kube events to S3: `aws s3 cp /tmp/canary-logs s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-9921/ --recursive`

oncall-sre: timeline so far: 02:11 release deployed -> 02:14 autopage triggered -> 02:15 traffic diverted -> 02:18 rollback started -> 02:25 canary scaled to 0 -> 02:30 stable verified.

pagerduty-bot: PD-9921 status -> resolved by oncall-sre. Closing incident after postmortem.

oncall-sre: marking incident as resolved. Please file a short postmortem with root cause: background worker triggering watchdog -> SIGTERM -> terminating canary pods. Include mitigation: traffic diversion + rollback.

maria: filing postmortem now and assigning action items: 1) revert commit + hard block on allocator touches in canary mode (owner: sam), 2) add automated test for watchdog behavior (owner: ashwin), 3) add stronger pre-release smoke for canary long-tail requests (owner: emily). ETA: 48h for PRs, 5d for tests.

sam: acked, starting on the revert.

oncall-sre: thanks everyone. Closing bridge. :white_check_mark:

ops-bridge-bot: bridge closed. Logs archived at https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-incident-logs/PD-9921/

incident-bot: Incident summary: PD-9921 | rt=~19m | impact=limited (0.02% traffic, short burst) | action=divert -> rollback -> scale-down | next=postmortem (PD-9921).
